rule: When drawing the jaw, keep in mind the lower plane of the jaw.
The facial features (eyes, nose and mouth) lie on lines that stay parallel to each other in perspective across the head.
The angles of the line across the eyes, the nostrils and the mouth line are parallel to one another.
The face can be simplified into an eye mask and a mouth mask to draw expressions.
The peaks of the upper and lower eyelid edges are offset from each other; aligning them horizontally looks static.
An iris seen at an angle is an asymmetrical ellipse where one side is wider or more curved than the other.
The mouth wraps around the curvature of the teeth, and a centre line divides the lips into quadrants defining top and bottom surfaces.
In profile, the face contour alternates convex and concave curves with crisp changes of direction; smoothing them out is a mistake.
The ear contains a Y-like shape, fits in a rectangle that shows its proportion, and has thickness.
